title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Country of Origin) Bill 2016
short_title: Competition and Consumer Amendment (Country of Origin) Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill changes the Australian Consumer Law to simplify the rules for using 'made in' claims on products.
It would clarify what counts as substantial transformation and remove the 50 per cent production cost test.
The bill is expected to have no financial impact, and the explanatory memorandum does not specify a start date for the changes.
changes: The bill amends the Australian Consumer Law to alter the definition of substantial transformation.
It removes the 50 per cent production cost test.
It clarifies that minor processes like dicing or canning do not justify a 'made in' claim.
summary.affected: Businesses making country of origin claims, particularly food businesses, and consumers who read these labels.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: The speaker moved the second reading of the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Country of Origin) Bill 2016, which aims to clarify safe harbour provisions in the Australian Consumer Law as part of a broader government reform package on country-of-origin labelling that includes a separate food labelling standard.
